payload.question_text: What format makes media analysis results predictable for later systems?

options.error_type: Confuses structured results with input content
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A scanned page image is source content, not a predictable structured result format.
options.better_fit: Use this as input when analyzing a document or image.

feedback.intrinsic: Later work would still require extracting the information from the image.
feedback.instructional: JSON results organize extracted fields for later use.

options.error_type: Confuses source media with analysis output
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An unprocessed recording is source media and has not been transformed into structured results.
options.better_fit: Use this as input for audio or video analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting details would remain locked in the recording.
feedback.instructional: Analysis produces structured JSON results from the recording.

options.rationale: This is correct. Predictable JSON results make extracted information easier for later systems to use.

options.error_type: Confuses structured output with manual processing
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A paper note is not a predictable structured format for system use.
options.better_fit: Use this for an informal human reminder, not for structured extracted results.

feedback.intrinsic: Searching and automating meeting details would be harder.
feedback.instructional: JSON supports storage, search, and automation.

payload.explanation: Correct—predictable JSON results are easier for later systems to use.

payload.question_text: Which fields can a conference-room camera image schema define? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Location is a field in the conference-room image schema.
This is correct. The schema can define the in-person attendee count.

options.error_type: Confuses meeting image fields with voicemail fields
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A callback number is a recorded-call field, not an attendance or location field for a camera image.
options.better_fit: Use this for voicemail analysis that extracts a caller's contact details.

feedback.intrinsic: The attendance view would include an unrelated call detail.
feedback.instructional: For a meeting image, focus on location and attendee counts.

options.rationale: This is correct. The schema can define the remote attendee count.

payload.explanation: Correct—location, in-person attendees, and remote attendees are image-schema fields.

payload.question_text: Structured media results cannot be searched after analysis.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A coordinator could miss useful meeting details later.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Structured results can be stored, searched, analyzed, and passed to later processes.

payload.explanation: Correct—structured results can be searched after analysis.

payload.question_text: The conference-room image returned three attendees in total.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: One attendee would be omitted from the meeting count.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Three is the remote count; one in-person attendee makes four total.

payload.explanation: Correct—the total was four, not three.

payload.question_text: What can video analysis extract from a recorded meeting?

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with document OCR
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Printed text is associated with OCR for documents and images, not the full range of meeting-video insights.
options.better_fit: Use this for a scanned page or receipt image when the goal is to read printed text.

feedback.intrinsic: The coordinator would miss attendance and follow-up actions.
feedback.instructional: Video analysis can capture meeting details beyond printed text.

options.rationale: This is correct. Video meeting analysis can extract attendance and assigned actions.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with voicemail extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A callback number is a call-detail field and does not represent the range of meeting details available from video.
options.better_fit: Use this for a voicemail schema that extracts contact details.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting review would focus on one call detail.
feedback.instructional: Callback numbers fit calls; video can also provide attendance and actions.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with invoice extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Totals and tax are invoice fields, not meeting details extracted from video.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing an invoice for billing amounts.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting record would not identify attendees or actions.
feedback.instructional: Invoice fields belong to invoice analysis; video can capture meeting information.

payload.explanation: Correct—video analysis can reveal attendance and assigned actions.

payload.question_text: Which statements correctly identify prebuilt-videoSearch? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. prebuilt-videoSearch is identified as a prebuilt analyzer.

options.error_type: Confuses video analyzer with invoice analyzer
options.rationale: This is incorrect. prebuilt-videoSearch is for video, while invoice analysis uses a prebuilt invoice analyzer.
options.better_fit: Use this statement for an invoice analyzer when the input is an invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: A video conference could be matched with the wrong analysis.
feedback.instructional: Match the analyzer to the input type: video uses prebuilt-videoSearch.

options.text: It is used for video input
options.rationale: This is correct. It is selected when the input is video.
This is correct. It is the prebuilt choice for video-related structured information.

payload.explanation: Correct—prebuilt-videoSearch is the prebuilt choice for video analysis.

payload.question_text: Azure Content Understanding can analyze recorded meetings and other video files.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Useful meeting details would be overlooked.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Video is a supported content type, including recorded meetings.

payload.explanation: Correct—recorded meetings and other media files can be analyzed as video.

payload.question_text: Which field belongs in a video recording schema?

options.rationale: This is correct. Assigned actions can be included in a video meeting schema.

options.error_type: Confuses meeting schema with invoice schema
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Invoice subtotal is a billing field and does not describe recorded meeting activity.
options.better_fit: Use this in an invoice schema that extracts billing amounts.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting record would not capture follow-up work.
feedback.instructional: Assigned actions fit a meeting schema; invoice subtotal fits an invoice.

options.error_type: Confuses meeting schema with invoice schema
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Vendor name is an invoice field, not a field listed for a video meeting schema.
options.better_fit: Use this when extracting information from an invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting review would miss follow-up work.
feedback.instructional: Choose fields that describe the meeting, such as assigned actions.

options.error_type: Confuses video meeting schema with voicemail schema
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A callback number is a voicemail contact field rather than a meeting-video field.
options.better_fit: Use this in a schema for a recorded voice message.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting review would focus on a call detail.
feedback.instructional: For a video meeting, include actions and other meeting details.

payload.explanation: Correct—a meeting video schema can include assigned actions.

payload.question_text: prebuilt-audioSearch is the prebuilt analyzer selected for video input.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A recorded video conference would be treated as the wrong media type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: For video input, select prebuilt-videoSearch rather than an audio analyzer.

payload.explanation: Correct—an audio analyzer is not selected for video input.

payload.question_text: A video meeting schema can include a summary of the discussion.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A reader would miss the meeting's main discussion points.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The schema can include a discussion summary as well as assigned actions.

payload.explanation: Correct—a discussion summary can be included in a video meeting schema.

metadata.unit_slo: Describe the information a video analyzer can extract from a meeting.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.
